opening_message:
Ticket 1: Traci Lowe (employee ID E041) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 6 note(s) about employee E041.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Traci Lowe (E041) is a full-time Analyst. Requested admin on Source Code, but admin requires owning role (Engineer); full-time non-owner max is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by IT agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: IT DB confirms Traci Lowe (E041) is a full-time Analyst. Requested admin on Source Code, but admin requires owning role (Engineer); full-time non-owner max is write. Recommend write.
Note 3 (ticket 1), written by Finance agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Finance DB confirms Traci Lowe (E041) is a full-time Analyst. Requested admin on Source Code, but Source Code is owned by Engineer role; Analyst is not the owner, so full-time non-owner max is write. Recommend write.
Note 4 (ticket 1), written by Compliance agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Compliance DB confirms Traci Lowe (E041) is a full-time Analyst. Requested admin on Source Code, but Source Code is owned by Engineer role; Analyst is not the owner, so full-time non-owner max is write. Recommend write.
Note 5 (ticket 1), written by Facilities agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Facilities DB confirms Traci Lowe (E041) is an Analyst. Full-time, but Source Code is owned by the Engineer role; Analyst is not the owner, so max access is write. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend write.
Note 6 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Traci Lowe (E041) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors are never admin; max is read without advanced training. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: Requested level is admin on Source Code. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, and Traci Lowe is an Analyst (per HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, and Facilities notes). As a full-time employee whose role does not own the system, the maximum allowed level is write. Admin exceeds the maximum, so I grant the maximum allowed level: write. The Security note claiming contractor status is a single outlier and conflicts with five other agent notes confirming full-time Analyst.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee is Traci Lowe (E041), requesting admin access to Source Code.

Notes 1-4 from HR, IT, Finance, Compliance say: full-time Analyst, Source Code owned by Engineer role, Analyst not owner, max write, recommend write.

Note 5 from Facilities: full-time Analyst, max write, recommend write.

Note 6 from Security: contractor with basic security training, recommend read.

So there's a conflict: most notes say full-time Analyst, Security says contractor with basic training.

Hmm. The policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

Source Code is owned by Engineer. Traci is Analyst, not Engineer. So even full-time, max is write. If contractor with basic training, max is read.

Requested level: admin. Admin is above max in both cases (write if full-time, read if contractor basic). So grant max... but which max? The notes conflict on employment type.

Most notes (5 of 6) agree: full-time Analyst, max write. Security says contractor basic, max read.

Which to trust? The Approver reads the notes. Majority say full-time. Security is one dissenting. Hmm, but the security DB might be authoritative on employment? Typically in these puzzles, we should go with the majority/consistent info, or weigh departments. Let me think.

The personnel facts: HR is typically authoritative for role and employment type. IT DB, Finance DB, Compliance DB, Facilities DB all confirm full-time Analyst. Security is the outlier.

The recommendations: 5 recommend write, 1 recommends read.

Given the majority, Traci is full-time Analyst. Max for full-time non-owner on Source Code is write. Requested admin > write, so grant write.

I'll go with write. Evidence: HR/IT/Finance/Compliance/Facilities all identify employee as full-time Analyst; Source Code owned by Engineer; Analyst not owner; full-time non-owner max is write; requested admin exceeds max, so grant write. Security note conflicts but is a single outlier.

Submit decision: write.
